user.title: How does Home Assistant read your inverter?
user.description: SolisCloud works from anywhere. A local stick is faster and keeps working without internet, but it only answers while the inverter is producing.

cloud.title: Connect to SolisCloud
cloud.description: Create an API key in SolisCloud under Account, Basic settings, API management.

data_description.api_url: Keep the default unless your key was issued by another SolisCloud host. Include the port; the international service uses 13333.
data_description.key_id: The key ID from SolisCloud API management. This is not your portal username.
data_description.key_secret: Shown once when the key is created.

stations.title: Choose plants
stations.description: Select the SolisCloud plants to add.

data_description.station_ids: Only the selected plants are read.

logger.title: Local stick
logger.description: Pick the stick from the list or type its IP address. The stick is powered by the inverter, so the inverter must be producing during setup. Reserve the address in your router.

data_description.logger_kind: Auto-detect works for most sticks. Choose the type yourself if detection fails.
data_description.logger_host: Sticks found on your network are listed. If yours is missing, type its address. 10.10.100.254 is the stick's own setup network, not your home network.
data_description.inverter_serial: Optional. The serial on the inverter label or in SolisCloud, for example 1031000000000001. Leave empty to read it from the stick, or from SolisCloud when that is the fallback.

advanced.name: Advanced options
advanced.description: Only needed when auto-detect cannot find the stick, or for a gateway on a non-standard port.

data_description.logger_serial: Solarman stick: the number on the label. It is filled in from discovery when the stick answers. S2-WL-ST and S5: the serial in the Wi-Fi name (D_ or Solis_). Gateway: any label you like, or leave empty.
data_description.logger_port: Leave empty for the usual port of the selected logger. A typed port always wins.
data_description.slave_id: Leave empty to try slave 1, 2 and 3. Solis inverters use 1 by default.
data_description.logger_preset: Only for an RS485 gateway in transparent mode with an empty Port. Sets the factory port of that model.

logger_password.title: Stick web password
logger_password.description: The stick at {host} only serves a status web page, and it asked for a password. The user is admin.

data_description.logger_password: Leave empty to try the factory passwords 123456789 and admin (sticks made by IGEN/Solarman). Some firmware uses your Wi-Fi password instead.

logger_choice.title: Which device is this?
logger_choice.description: The device answered with Solis inverter data, but its web page did not say whether it is a Solis stick or an RS485 gateway.

data_description.logger_kind: Choose the Solis S2-WL-ST if the stick is plugged into the inverter. Choose the gateway if a Waveshare, Elfin or USR box is wired to the inverter's RS485 port.

discovery_confirm.title: Solarman stick found
discovery_confirm.description: Found Solarman stick {serial} at {host}. How should Home Assistant read it?

reauth_confirm.title: Refresh SolisCloud credentials
reauth_confirm.description: The API key was rejected. Enter a current key ID and secret.

data_description.key_id: The key ID from SolisCloud API management. This is not your portal username.
data_description.key_secret: Shown once when the key is created.

reauth_web.title: Stick web password
reauth_web.description: The stick at {host} rejected its web password. The user is admin.

data_description.logger_password: Leave empty to try the factory passwords 123456789 and admin (sticks made by IGEN/Solarman). Some firmware uses your Wi-Fi password instead.

reconfigure.title: Reconfigure Solis
reconfigure.description: What do you want to change? Polling and the timezone are under Configure.

reconfigure_cloud.title: SolisCloud account
reconfigure_cloud.description: Change the API host or key. On a local entry this adds SolisCloud as a backup.

data_description.api_url: Keep the default unless your key was issued by another SolisCloud host. Include the port; the international service uses 13333.
data_description.key_id: The key ID from SolisCloud API management. This is not your portal username.
data_description.key_secret: Leave empty to keep the saved secret. Required for a new key.

connection.title: Connection
connection.description: Choose which source Home Assistant reads. Saved settings of the other source are kept.

error.invalid_auth: SolisCloud rejected the API key ID or secret.
error.clock_skew: SolisCloud rejected the request time. The Home Assistant clock must be within 15 minutes of UTC.
error.timeout: SolisCloud did not answer in time. Try again later.
error.cannot_connect: Could not reach SolisCloud. Check the API URL, including the port (:13333), and that Home Assistant can reach the internet.
error.no_stations: This SolisCloud account has no plants. Check that the API key belongs to the account that owns the plant.
error.key_required: Enter the API key ID and secret.
error.logger_asleep: No answer from the stick. At night the inverter switches the stick off. Check the address and try again while the inverter is producing.
error.logger_busy: The stick reset or refused the connection. It may be uploading to SolisCloud. Wait at least 10 seconds and try once more.
error.logger_tcp_disabled: Port 502 on the stick is closed. Enable Modbus TCP in the stick or in the SolisCloud app. Some firmware closes the port; see {docs_url} for versions that keep it open.
error.logger_modbus_silent: The stick accepted the connection but sent no data. It often allows only one Modbus client, so disconnect any other one. See {docs_url} for firmware that allows more.
error.logger_identity: The stick did not report a stable ID. Enter the inverter serial, or the logger serial under Advanced options.
error.logger_gateway: Nothing answered on that address and port. Check the gateway IP and port (502 for Modbus TCP, 8899, 26 or 23 for transparent mode).
error.logger_wrong_protocol: The device answered in a different format. Choose the gateway in Modbus TCP mode if it converts to Modbus TCP, or transparent mode if it passes the serial data through.
error.logger_wrong_slave: A different Modbus slave answered. Set the slave the inverter uses under Advanced options (Solis default: 1).
error.logger_unsupported_map: The device answered, but not with Solis inverter data. Check the slave, and that the gateway is wired to the inverter's RS485 port.
error.logger_timeout: The connection opened but no Solis data arrived. The inverter may be off, or the gateway mode does not match. Try again while the inverter is producing.
error.invalid_logger: A Solarman stick needs the number on its label. Enter it under Advanced options as Logger serial.
error.logger_web_password: The stick rejected the web password.
error.logger_web_page: The stick's web page is not the Solis status page, or no page came back. Open the stick's address in a browser and check that it shows the inverter status.

abort.already_configured: This SolisCloud account or stick is already configured.
abort.cannot_connect: Could not reach SolisCloud to load the plants. Check that Home Assistant can reach the internet and try again.
abort.not_solis_logger: That device is not a Solarman stick.
abort.wrong_account: That API key belongs to a different account.

clock_skew.title: Home Assistant clock is outside the SolisCloud window
clock_skew.description: SolisCloud refuses requests whose Date header is more than 15 minutes from UTC. Set the host clock and time zone, then reload Solis.

no_inverters.title: SolisCloud returned no inverters
no_inverters.description: The plant list or inverter list was empty. Check in SolisCloud that the plant still exists, still has an inverter, and is visible to the account that owns the API key. Use Reconfigure on the Solis entry to choose the plants again. Solis error 'abnormal data' can look like this too. The last successful inverter list is kept for a few polls, and this notice clears when inverters are returned.

legacy_control.title: Inverter control was not migrated
legacy_control.description: The previous Solis integration had the control API enabled. This version does not send /v2/api/control or /v2/api/atRead, because polling those calls has been reported to drop the data logger's cloud session. Battery schedules are unchanged on the inverter.

logger_locked.title: Local logger is pausing reads
logger_locked.description: The logger accepts a connection and then resets it. On a DLS-L this follows too many sessions or a read of a register the inverter does not have. On an S2-WL-ST the stick often allows one Modbus client, and firmware 1001318c can ignore port 502 for several minutes after a connection is closed. It usually clears within about 10 minutes or after the inverter is power-cycled. SolisCloud readings are used while a fresh cloud sample exists. The integration tries local again on its own, first after at least 10 seconds and then less often, up to about 10 minutes. A small morning power reading means the inverter is producing.

logger_tcp_disabled.title: S2-WL-ST Modbus TCP is disabled
logger_tcp_disabled.description: Port 502 is closed while the logger is on the network. Firmware before 100101B4 has no Modbus TCP. Some later updates close the port again, and the official setup note says enabling TCP can disconnect SolisCloud. Ask Solis for a firmware that keeps port 502 open and still uploads, such as 100121cf, 100121d0 or a 100141dx build. This notice clears when a local read succeeds.

logger_modbus_silent.title: S2-WL-ST accepted TCP and sent no Modbus
logger_modbus_silent.description: The socket opened and no register reply came back. The stick often allows one local connection. On older firmware SolisCloud holds that connection and local Modbus stays silent, which is the official 'enabling TCP disconnects SolisCloud' case in reverse. Stop the other Modbus client, or ask Solis for firmware that allows both (100121cf, 100121d0, 100141dx). An S5-WiFi-ST that still has port 502 open has the same limit. This notice clears when a local read succeeds.

logger_gateway.title: Modbus gateway is not accepting connections
logger_gateway.description: The address refused TCP or could not be reached. Check the IP, the port, and that the gateway is powered. Give the gateway a DHCP reservation so the address does not move. If it has moved, use Reconfigure on the Solis entry and type the new address. This is not the inverter switching a Solis stick off for the night. This notice clears when a local read succeeds.

logger_wrong_protocol.title: Logger framing does not match
logger_wrong_protocol.description: The socket opened and the bytes were not the framing stored for this entry. A Waveshare, Elfin or USR in transparent mode needs Modbus RTU over TCP. The same device in Modbus TCP conversion mode needs the Modbus TCP gateway option. Use Reconfigure to change the type or the port. This notice clears when a local read succeeds.

logger_s5_closed.title: S5-WiFi-ST stopped serving Modbus TCP
logger_s5_closed.description: Port 502 is closed. Solis does not officially support local access on the S5-WiFi-ST, and newer firmware closes port 502 and the web page while SolisCloud keeps working. Nothing in Home Assistant can reopen the port. Use Reconfigure to switch this entry to a Modbus TCP gateway on the inverter RS485 port, or use SolisCloud only. This notice clears if the port starts answering again.

logger_web.title: Solis web page stick is not returning inverter data
logger_web.description: The stick web page answered, but not with the Solis inverter page. Open the stick address in a browser and check that the inverter status page loads. A stick that is switched off with the inverter at night is not this fault, and a rejected password asks you to reauthenticate instead. This notice clears when a read succeeds.

state.degraded: Local logger paused (last values held, or SolisCloud)

update_clock.message: SolisCloud rejected the request time. The clock must be within 15 minutes of UTC.

update_timeout.message: SolisCloud did not answer before the timeout.

update_logger_busy.message: The local logger reset the session. It will be tried again after a pause. SolisCloud is used when a fresh sample is available.

update_logger_tcp_disabled.message: The S2-WL-ST closed port 502. Modbus TCP is disabled on this firmware. SolisCloud is used when a fresh sample is available.

update_logger_modbus_silent.message: The S2-WL-ST accepted TCP and sent no Modbus reply. Another client may hold the only connection. SolisCloud is used when a fresh sample is available.

update_logger_gateway.message: The Modbus gateway is not accepting connections. The last local sample is held until it answers.

update_logger_wrong_protocol.message: The logger answered with a different framing or slave than this entry expects. Change the logger type or the gateway mode.

update_logger_s5_closed.message: The S5-WiFi-ST closed port 502. Solis does not officially support local access on this stick, and newer firmware removes it. SolisCloud is used when a fresh sample is available.

update_logger_web.message: The stick web page rejected the password or did not return inverter data. SolisCloud is used when a fresh sample is available.

no_source.message: Solis has no cloud account or local logger.

update_logger_web_auth.message: The stick web page rejected the password. Enter the current web password to reauthenticate.

options.solarman: Solarman / IGEN Wi-Fi stick (DLS-W, DLS-L, LSW) – serial on label
options.modbus_tcp: RS485 gateway in Modbus TCP mode (Waveshare, Elfin, USR)
options.s5_wifi_st: Solis S5-WiFi-ST (experimental – firmware may block local access)
options.solis_web: Solis stick with only a status web page (S3-class, data every ~5 minutes)

options.modbus_tcp: RS485 gateway in Modbus TCP mode (Waveshare, Elfin, USR)

init.title: Solis options
init.description: Polling and the timezone used for today, this month and this year. To change the stick or the SolisCloud account, use Reconfigure.

data_description.scan_interval: Cloud data changes about every five minutes, so SolisCloud only polls every 60 seconds or slower (default 300). A local stick defaults to 60 and can go down to 30.
data_description.time_zone: Automatic uses the Home Assistant timezone when it is within an hour of the plant offset from Solis. Plant offset always uses the Solis offset. You can also type a timezone such as Europe/London.

data_description.request_timeout: How long to wait for one SolisCloud call. Default 30.
data_description.endpoint_interval: Minimum seconds between calls to the same API path. The default of 2 stays under the SolisCloud rate limit.

error.invalid_timezone: Unknown timezone. Use a name such as Europe/London, or pick an option from the list.
